chapter: Kid Ory, Hampton, Ellington and Ben Webster
title: Hampton's underpayment, again
summary: Mingus repeats the $400 versus $125 story and says he was never paid for arrangements.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing in Lionel Hampton's big band

blocks.x: You were with Hampton. And there's a kind of a -- sort of a public image with Hampton as a happy go lucky, not especially bright guy that could swing good. Is

No. He's a very dishonest man, and his wife -- he and his wife made millions of dollars off of hiring unknown musicians out in the sticks for little or no money, promise them one salary, get them out on the road and says, Lionel Hampton has the right to promise that kind of money. I was promised -- Lionel guaranteed me $400 a week when I first joined the band. And so I got on the road, I was very far away from California, and Gladys Hampton called to me and he says, why, we could pay that kind of money. No one -- Milt Buckner doesn't get that kind of money. But they didn't do that until they took us on the road. I kept getting these small checks, I said, what is this? $125 a week on the road.
Gee, and you had to pay your other stuff besides.
That was his wife Gladys, as I remember.
They never paid me for arrangements, Mingus Fingers or nothing.
